data.description:
## Finding (audit of epic 3405-c0b7)
**Site:** the gate degrade producers in `src/rebar/llm/workflow/gate_dispatch.py` — `_degraded_plan_review_verdict` (via the `except (LLMUnavailableError, LLMInputRejectedError)` arm at line 203), `_degraded_code_review_verdict` (line ~336 sets `"llm_unavailable": True`), and the completion-verdict degrade. They emit `coverage.llm_unavailable = True`.

**Problem:** the arm catches `(LLMUnavailableError, LLMInputRejectedError)` together (comment at line 203 folds `LLMInputRejectedError`, bug 43d4, into "the mid-run infra outage" arm). So when the cause is an INPUT REJECTION (oversized/malformed prompt, content-policy refusal), the verdict still carries `coverage.llm_unavailable=True`. The field's docstring admits the name is overloaded to mean "no provider record accompanies this verdict" (degraded), NOT literally "the provider is down".

**Wrong signal:** `coverage.llm_unavailable=True` for a non-availability fault. `resolution_fields(outcome)` DOES ride the truthful `resolution_class` (CHANGE_INPUT) alongside, so the disposition is recoverable — but the boolean's NAME misreports the cause.

**Consumers that branch on the boolean:** `plan_review/drift_floor.py:202`, `plan_review/orchestrator.py:468`, `review_bot/adapter.py:114`.

**Observable vs latent:** OBSERVABLE — on every degraded gate verdict JSON and to the three consumers above.

**Proposed fix (needs decision):** behavior-change / rename — either split the flag (a neutral `degraded` / `no_provider_record` boolean vs a strict `llm_unavailable` reserved for real outages) or have consumers/readers key off `resolution_class` instead of the overloaded boolean. Affects the verdict contract and three consumers → **escalate**.

**caused_by / class:** the same "input-rejection framed as provider outage" pattern; origin 8a31 / bug 43d4.
data.title: Gate degrade sets coverage.llm_unavailable=True for LLMInputRejectedError (overloaded/misleading boolean)
